verdict_reason: Paging logic is correct and tested against the ACs (8 a page, no pagination at one page, query and selection carried), but the first-page constant has three homes and a single-use literal and internal doc comments break house rules.

todos.issue: The first page number is declared three times in one picker folder: FIRST_PAGE = 1 in pagination/index.js:7, pagination/page-numbers.js:1 and view-model/results-href.js:4. Each one decides where paging starts (index.js:11,19,40; page-numbers.js:6,11; results-href.js:15 leaves page off the link on the first page), so a change to it in one file leaves the others disagreeing.
todos.fix: Must: one module in the party-picker owns the first page number, and pagination/index.js, page-numbers.js and results-href.js all read it from there. One way: export FIRST_PAGE from one small module (for example pagination/first-page.js, which avoids a cycle with results-href.js) and import it in the other three files, deleting their local copies; mirror the same in the plants twin's address-book-picker/pagination.js.

todos.issue: MINIMUM_PAGES_TO_PAGINATE (line 8) sits at module scope but only paginationLinks (line 33) reads it. The house rule puts a literal used by one function inside that function.
todos.fix: Must: the two-page threshold lives inside paginationLinks, and module scope holds only values the module shares or a test imports. One way: move the MINIMUM_PAGES_TO_PAGINATE declaration into the body of paginationLinks, and do the same in the plants twin's address-book-picker/pagination.js.

todos.issue: Doc comments on feature-internal helpers: line 4 above ADDRESSES_A_PAGE restates the name, and lines 13-14 above servedPageOf explain what the name means (the last page when the request is past it). These are not a public API, and a comment that decodes a name means the name or a test should carry it.
todos.fix: Must: no doc comments on these feature-internal exports; the clamping is stated by the servedPageOf tests (or a name that says it), not a comment. One way: delete the comments at lines 4 and 13-14 (and the one at 26-27 if the reviewer agrees it is internal too), keeping index.test.js 'Should serve the last page when the list stops short of the page asked for' as the statement of the rule; mirror in the plants twin.
